newsitem.title: ROMANIA: One dead, hundreds evacuated in Romania floods.
newsitem.headline: One dead, hundreds evacuated in Romania floods.

text.p: Rivers throughout Romania spilled their banks at the weekend, killing one man and prompting the evacuation of thousands of people, officials said on Monday.

One man drowned in the Vaslui region near the border with ex-Soviet Moldova when his horse-drawn cart was carried off by floodwaters, the environment ministry said. It added that 315 households had been ordered to leave to higher ground.

Three days of incessant rain pushed up the levels of 17 small rivers in the western Banat region near ex-Yugoslavia, Crisana near the Hungarian border, in central Transylvania and in eastern regions near Moldova and the River Danube.
In the worst-hit area of Banat, television pictures showed water from heavy downpours cascading down streets in the town of Resita, carrying away cars.
Flooding last month killed 12 people in the region of Bihor, near the Hungarian border.
The ministry said 1,000 hectares of farmland were now under water, but government officials have insisted in the past week that the grain harvest has been unaffected by bad weather.
Weather forecasters said they expected better weather in coming days, with rainfall restricted to mountain areas.
On the Danube, meteorologists said there was little danger of flooding, but flows were registered at 50 percent higher than normal levels and were expected to rise further.
